Dmitri: Reproducer ready for the long-stream memory ramp I'm seeing in the staging toolloop. Minimal steps: run toolloop with --streaming --max-seq=8192 against the new kernel-selection branch. After ~90m mem keeps climbing. Attaching quick traces below and a tiny flame snippet.

Dmitri: Repro command: `./tools/run_toolloop --profile --streaming --workers=8 --max-seq=8192 --prefetch=0`

Dmitri: Key observation: resident set increases even when active session count is flat. Heap snapshots show KV page residency growing in a narrow set of slabs. `/var/tmp/heapshots/heap-90m.pb.gz` is the pprof upload.

Ben: :eyes: can you paste the small metric dump? pinned_pages / kv_alloc_slab numbers?

Dmitri: Quick dump (after 2h):
```
kv_total_pages: 6,214,112
kv_pinned_pages: 1,204,992  # monotonic increase from 80k
kv_page_walks: 3,421,334
eviction_passes: 12
page_fragmentation_ratio: 1.34
```
Memory delta ~+3.6GB from kv_pinned_pages.

Alice: That pinned_pages jump is suspicious. Did the new kernel-selection path change page-aliasing or fallback kernels that disable fast-evict?

Dmitri: Possibly. The failing runs were on the branch that introduced `select_kernel_for_seq()` heuristics (fallback to generic for >4k). I instrumented the kernel path with a counter: generic_kernel_fallbacks: 87k. Also see increased `page_lock_time_ms` in samplers.

Carol: Two quick hypotheses: 1) eviction not called because page pinned by ongoing streaming sessions (KV pin + streaming toolloop holding refs), 2) pagewalks trigger short-lived pinning then fail to release due to error path introduced in fallback. Any stack traces from when pinned_pages increments?

Dmitri: I captured a short CPU profile around a spike. Link: `s3://redwood-profiles/3087654321/pprof-cpu-120s.svg`

perf-bot: auto-report: Heap growth slope = +28 MB / 10m over 3 hours. Top heap alloc site: kv_page_map::insert_ref (42%), kv_pin::retain (31%), background_evictor::scan_single (9%).

Ben: If background_evictor isn't reclaiming because it thinks pages are in-use, maybe reference counting lost an unlock on fallback code. Check `kv_pin::release()` call paths in the new kernel selection (`select_kernel_for_seq`) — especially early returns.

Alice: Also confirm batching heuristics: if we increased per-request batch size, KV reuse patterns change. Larger batches keep more prefixes hot. What's real batch distribution in the reproducer?

Dmitri: Distribution: median batch=8, 95p=32, tail occasional 128 when toolloop batches coalesce. Behavior consistent with prod-ish tail.

Carol: Can you grep for `goto fail` or `return` paths in the fallback block? Historically those are where we miss release sequences. Small snippet might help.

Dmitri: Snippet from select_kernel_for_seq (simplified):
```
if (seq_len > KERNEL_THRESH) {
  kernel = generic_kernel;
  if (!generic_supported()) {
    return ERR_UNSUPPORTED;  // <-- potential missing release upstream?
  }
}
```
I see a few callers that assume non-null kernel and skip cleanup when ERR_UNSUPPORTED returned.

Ben: That fits. Caller should unwind kv_pin on error. Which callers are we hitting? Use `rg "select_kernel_for_seq\(" -n` across runtime.

Dmitri: Ran a quick search: `runtime/streamer/stepper.cc:142`, `runtime/toolchain/runloop.cc:88`. Both have early returns on kernel error.

perf-bot: quick patch suggestion (non-prod): wrap kernel select with RAII that ensures kv_pin.release() on all exits. Perf impact negligible in local tests.

Alice: Before code changes, can we produce a minimal unit test that exercises the error path? Maybe mock generic_supported()=false and assert pinned_pages returns to baseline after run. If that repro is fast we'll be confident.

Dmitri: Agree. I pushed a unit test branch `kv-backpressure/fix-unwind` with a failing test that replicates pinned_pages not returning. CI log: `CI: test_kv_unwind: failed -> pinned_pages +1200`.

Carol: Nice. Once you have the test passing, let's run a long 6h staging run with the fix and the new kernel heuristics enabled. Also add a metric alert for pinned_pages growth > 500k in 1h so oncall gets paged earlier.

Dmitri: Oncall-bot FYI: deployment `canary/kv-backpressure/3087654321` triggered staging run.

oncall-bot: mentioned_in: #eng-runtime, incident_id: none, run_id: canary/kv-backpressure/3087654321, alert_target: eng-runtime-oncall

Ben: One more angle: batching may change KV cache locality and increase page fragmentation (page_fragmentation_ratio >1.3). Consider adding a background compaction pass every N minutes to coalesce partially used pages. That would be complementary to fix.

Dmitri: Plan: 1) land unwind fix in `kv-backpressure/fix-unwind` (PR up), 2) add unit test for error-path pinned-pages, 3) run 6h staging and collect heap snapshots every 30m, 4) evaluate introducing compaction if growth persists.

Alice: @Dmitri add the compaction opt-in flag behind `--kv-compaction` so we can A/B test. Also record kernel-selection fallback rates in metrics.

Dmitri: Will do. Thanks all — I'll update thread with CI green + staging results. :thumbsup:

Carol: :clap: good sleuthing.
